svg.title: .NET and C# ecosystem explained for Python developers
svg.desc: A layered structural diagram showing how .NET, C#, the CLR, and various app frameworks relate to each other, with Python analogies throughout.

g.text: ≈ same as in Python — your OS sits at the bottom
Manages memory (GC), JIT-compiles IL to native code, runs .NET apps
≈ CPython interpreter — the engine that actually executes your code
BCL (Base Class Library) + runtime + tooling — ≈ Python standard library + pip ecosystem

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Tell me more about the .NET BCL (Base Class Library)')
sendPrompt('What is NuGet and how does it compare to pip?')

svg.text: Today just say ".NET" — .NET Framework is old and mostly legacy enterprise.
≈ Python 2 vs Python 3 — same idea, use the modern one
Languages that compile to IL (Intermediate Language) and run on the CLR:

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Give me a quick intro to C# syntax for a Python developer')
sendPrompt('What is ASP.NET Core and how does it compare to FastAPI or Django?')
sendPrompt('What is ML.NET and when would I use it?')
sendPrompt('What are .NET Worker Services and background jobs?')

svg.text: Click any box to ask a follow-up question ↗
C# is the language • .NET is the platform • CLR is the runtime — they always come as a bundle
